name: MolmoSpaces
summary: MolmoSpaces is AI2's open ecosystem for embodied evaluation: over 230,000 indoor environments, from handcrafted household scenes to procedurally generated multi-room houses, populated with 130,000 annotated object assets including 48,000 manipulable objects carrying 42 million precomputed stable grasps. MolmoSpaces-Bench sits on top and is built around controlled variation — object shape, size, weight and articulation; layout and clutter; task complexity from single-step to hierarchical; lighting and viewpoint; friction and mass; and instruction phrasing — so a generalization claim can be attributed to an axis instead of a vibe. It reports strong sim-to-real correlation (R = 0.96), and its evaluation surfaced policy sensitivities to prompt phrasing, initial joint configuration and camera occlusion. Assets, tooling and multiple simulator backends are open.
innovation: Generalization measured one controlled axis at a time, rather than as a single aggregate success rate.
Scale of annotated manipulable assets — 42M precomputed stable grasps — that makes procedural task generation practical.
Reports the sim-to-real correlation instead of assuming it, which is what licenses using the sim score at all.
matters: The strongest answer yet to why simulated benchmark numbers should be believed, and it is fully open where the leading alternatives are vendor infrastructure.
limits: Indoor household scenes; industrial and outdoor settings are out of scope.
R = 0.96 is measured over the policies tested, and need not hold for architectures unlike them.
lineage: BEHAVIOR-1K and RoboCasa's simulated-household lineage at an order more scale, with Molmo's grounding work behind the annotation.
